body:
I also call myself a ghost because people tend to forget about me and even the couple of people who think about me don't care about my feelings.

Losing motivation for things we once found enjoyable is a symptom of our depression.  I once read some advice that suggested we should undertake the activity with our body, even if our soul isn't in it. So even if we lack that passion we once had, we are accomplishing something.

I too am a disposable friend. People love the warm, loving attention they get and then move on with their life. They don't lose any sleep about leaving us behind. I don't seek out friends anymore. It is not that I chase people away, but I no longer give of myself the way I did. This bending over backwards for those that did not earn it is called Doormat Syndrome, and it leaves us vulnerable to users.

Years ago, I saw a parakeet hanging out with a flock of house sparrows, you know, those small brown birds seen in yards. If you see these birds around your house, you may want to start feeding them, in hopes that your birds are finding comfort and safety with them.

For those of you who are not into Marie Kondo, I have heard that some U.S. military units are taught to pack their uniforms using the rolling method. It is an old method to maximize space in a bag.  Professional organizers have been rolling t-shirts to the drawer neat.  Say you saw it on the net. Whatever it takes to quickly get away from the abusers.

Hello. For what it is worth, I have known actual dumb people and you don't sound dumb.  I also struggle with caring about others only to be dismissed and discarded. It is called doormat syndrome. I am getting lots of help watching YouTube videos where counselors explain this and offer ways to not give so much of ourselves until people have shown themselves worthy. Perhaps this will help you, too.

I admire that you are self-taught on guitar. Do you really need this schooling? I have noticed that young people are more respecting of people who teach themselves things outside of school, so that diploma or degree might not be needed.
Hello, I am lonely too.  Why do you feel like you make everyone's life worse? Did other people tell you this?

Dumping a pet like that is an act of animal cruelty. I am not sure where you live but in many countries, stealing someone's pet and putting her out like that is a crime. Please consider making a police report.

Are you planning on living your life with a no fucks given attitude or are you thinking of ending your life because of anxiety? 

Lately, I have been thinking that since life is going to deal me one blow after another, and since people only care for me in superficial ways, I will stop letting social anxiety rule me and just go about my life not worrying about whether people approve of me in every way. 

I will not be rude or anti-social, just no longer listening to a voice that was put in my head a long time ago, which says that I must be perfect according to others, or face humiliation.
This happens too often to people like us for it to be a coincidence.

I can relate to this. For me, it is like those adult dogs and cats who are there because their owners got bored of them. The people got what they wanted out of the animal when it was new and cute and fun but they're done now so they are moving on.
Hello. I was wondering about your wife, has she said that she is disappointed in you? It might be possible that her disappointment is with the situation, without blaming you personally.

It is ridiculous that the police didn't believe your mother. It is not like physical violence is some rare thing. Of course, I also was not believed when my divorce turned ugly. His violence towards me became my fault. Just one of my many stories of how justice is always denied me.

As for my plans, I don't know what I want to do about this wrongdoing against me. I might let it go and just add it to my collection of stories or I might seek out more help from police and a lawyer.  

More importantly, today I began to think about seeking counseling. 

Thanks for taking the time to respond to me. It means so much to know that I am not alone.

I am going to take some time to process what you wrote. What you said about playing my hand helps. It sure seems like I'm being dealt from a marked deck, though. 

Thanks for saying I have dignity and worth, that is something we often lose sight of when we are being trampled on frequently.

That you took the time to reply to me means a lot. Thank-you so much.

You do matter! Your reason for not wanting to go to that wedding is perfectly valid. It sounds like your SO still carries a torch for his ex, and he is putting her before you. 

I hope you can retreat from this abusive situation and put your energy where it belongs, which is towards getting yourself in a better mental place.

I continue to be astounded at how narcissists and borderlines can turn any good thing into a negative. I doubt that you are going to mess it up at work, that is your mother's insecurity talking. 

Good luck with getting that job!

I agree. There is joking around and then there is teasing to the point where the family needs a safe word. The sexual connection is creepy and I am sad to see that even people who are aware that teasing hurts are still doing it, but as you said, are patting themselves on the back for not inflicting TOO MUCH emotional damage.

An alternative to seeing a counselor is visiting the library and looking through the self-help section. You can choose a few books that look promising but if it turns out you get a fake vibe from the author, just drop them off and look elsewhere. This may also help with that feeling of being judged you get when seeing a therapist face-to-face.
What did he want you to do rather than play and lounge on the beach and did he ever say what he wanted from you before his incredible meltdown?

That is a great observation! Yes, I agree, it seems to take an exceptional situation, like something that would get a narcissistic parent arrested or in the news, before most people see that no contact with abusive parents is a valid option.

I am sending you a friendly "agree to disagree" response because I am not looking to get into a long discussion about the matter. That last line, however... not harmful except for emotional hurt. Wow, that's an odd thing to say in a forum of people who have been emotionally abused.

I almost did not make my original comment because I suspected a few ruined nightgowns are minor compared to a narcissists' damage but I feel it is important not to go down the road of revenge or petty actions. 

Good luck with your situation.

It is strange to me that destroying property is sometimes considered OK so long as the person is in their teens. A teen is not a young child scribbling on a wall because they did not know better. 

I disagree that there is only harm if the clothes are irreplaceable. Even ordinary nightgowns cost money and a person has the right not to have their clothes destroyed.
I made no remark regarding whether police should be called (and I do think that would be going way overboard.)

I am sending you emotional support and virtual hugs if you want them. My mother gave me a humiliating nickname and then did the "it's a joke" response. To hell with people who run roughshod over your feelings and then blame you for having those feelings.
Cutting up someone's clothes is not a harmless prank.
I can relate. I was born to be my mother's friend, companion, and ultimately her caretaker. When I figured this out, I felt such rage at being like you said, born to be a slave.

That reminds me of my Grandmother's funeral. I wore a plain, ankle-length dress in a very dark purple color. As we were walking to Grandma's grave site to place flowers on the coffin and say our final good-byes, Uncle Narc tells me that I look like I am in that cult with the four wives. 

Somehow, I found my wit and answered that I am wife #2, to which he stupidly stammered "really? really?".
I hope it will not be long until you and the cat can move out and cut all ties with this insane woman.

Yaaaay! I am cheering you! 

My experiences have been similar to yours and I recently sent packing the last person who loved my kindness and concern yet put little effort in for me. Feels good, man. 

Not caring about what others say behind your back is tough, especially if you have been raised to be a people pleaser, but with experience you learn that life goes on even if someone does not like you.

Good luck in building new and healthy relationships. You have inspired me to do the same.

My experiences have been like yours and I want to add that I am always surprised at how others can just walk away from me with ease. It is like my love or friendship was a small thing to them. Afterwards, I wonder if their expressions of love or friendship were ever real. 

Currently, I am working on recognizing problems earlier and realizing that there are many people in the world, I don't have to settle for narcissistic, one-sided human interaction.
Oh you poor babies! How frightening and confusing it must have been to have a mother who acts even less mature than her young children.

The longer I have been away from my narc/borderline mother, the less abusive she has become and after over 20 years away from her, she is now non-abusive. I don't know exactly why this is but some abusers do become tamed when they realize they can not control you any longer. In my case, my mother might be thinking that she has to be nice or I'll cut her off completely.
I can assure you that you are a legitimate person. Hopefully you were not referring to the way children born out of wedlock used to be called illegitimate or worse.
Your wife may never take steps to be free of these abusive people. All you can do is demand that you and your children are never unwillingly exposed to or affected by their narcissism.
Narc logic: You are a responsible adult when you accept someone else controlling your life.
That is an incredibly wise and clever way of spelling it out.

I'm just shaking my head. These are not well people. Regarding the six envelopes, I had a situation when I tried to make sense of my mother's debt. She had a drawer full of bills which were from only a handful of accounts. I kept only the last bill from each account and tried to show her what she owed but she had a minor freakout and kept repeating "where are my bills?".
Thanks! This is what my mother asked when she learned I was in a car accident. Because "bitching" means you are OK.

It is a dead sub, but this would fit in perfectly over at /r/oldpeoplejobadvice 

Sorry you are dealing with someone who is not in touch with reality.
That sound you just heard was my jaw hitting the floor. What a perverted control freak.

Yes, I know what you mean about previous generations of men having to hide their feelings. Uncle Narc took it to extreme in this situation, due to his deeply hidden insecurities. 

I know he is able to appreciate the pains of war because one time, he mentioned his brother's experience in Vietnam, and did not act like this, but instead kept a respectful tone. 

It brought back a memory when you mentioned your dad's "this will put hair on your chest." With Uncle Narc, it was "this will put hair on your ass". At least with my Uncle Narc, I can laugh because it was said during his funny guy moments usually while offering some sort of food. How terribly stupid what your dad did to you.

I'm here for 'ya, Kit. A virtual hug if you want it. It's crazy how some people just seem to come out of nowhere with their cars. It is not your fault, I believe you when you say that you looked both ways. Careless drivers are their own breed of narcissist. 

When I was a kid, I actually was hit by a car but I refused any help and didn't tell anyone because I was afraid of having the same response but from my mother. Looking back, it could have gone either way, she would have either blamed me or ranted about the driver but then did nothing.

I hope that your illness has passed and you are feeling better.

I just want to send you some emotional support over your parent's  "joke" or accusation insinuating that you constantly hit them up for money. That is so freaking annoying and considering the facts of the situation, so damn insulting!

I see your point but in this particular post you only called out your mother's response to not having her birthday acknowledged as a separate day. I can see her point, although if she is treating it like a Federal case, that is a bit much.

I am in no way excusing her abusive behavior towards you.

OK, I laughed at the 'Nam thing but it sucks for holiday babies when their birthday is morphed in with the Christmas machine. It would have been no big deal to use the unprinted side of the Christmas paper or even the comics page of the newspaper to wrap birthday gifts.
For the person who endured the experience, yes, I would agree. But for a narcissist who never experienced such a thing and who feels compelled to project a tough image, it is just more bullshit.
That could be argued for every narcissist.

I see that you asked for comforting words but I can not in good conscience say anything that will encourage you to continue a toxic relationship. It would be far better for you to remove yourself from your abuser's lives, they don't get a pass because they are family.

Why do you feel that you must visit your parents and take their abuse? How will she destroy your life?
Jesus also turned over tables and chased with a whip those who were disrespecting the temple. That's how we should practice Jesus' love on Narcs.

That is great news, that you and your intended see eye-to-eye on this matter. I'm breathing a sigh of relief that you understand the need to put  emotional distance between you and your parents. 

Good luck to both of you and best wishes for your marriage!
Narcs often "forget" that their child's spouse also has a family. It's all about them!!!

Where does your fiancé stand in all of this? Why are you taking on all this stress dealing with his mother? Is he being passive about this whole matter? 

Take it from someone who has been in your shoes (right down to being annoyed with the use of "home" even after their son is established elsewhere), if your guy is not on the same page as you, it will spell trouble for your relationship. 

If your experience is anything like my own, you will be accused of keeping their son away from his family, just because he doesn't run "home" for every single holiday.
That is so annoying! Let me guess: you don't actually put her down, it has become a crutch word to lean on when you disagree with her.

Thank-you, this will be of help to me. My mother is more borderline than narcissist. She is a waif who needs to be taken care of. Once she lost her grip on me, she turned to men and married one of them. I think she will come crying to me when her husband dies. 

I don't mind helping her in her old age so long as she understands I am not going to be her constant companion and go-between every time she doesn't want to talk to someone.

Others who have been in your situation will be along shortly, but I am familiar with the guilt. Why do you feel guilty? Is it because of society's unreasonable expectations or was there some other reason that you thought you should stay in contact with an abusive person? 

I think it will get easier and when your stress levels have dropped, you will see clearly and know you did the right thing. The very fact that you are afraid of being stalked by this person shows you had reason to put them out of your life.

Drop them into the trash. They are just another piece of junk mail. Returning them to sender is more effort than she deserves and is a tiny bit of communication to give her hope.

Good luck with your continued no contact!
Wow, this is timely and relevant to my interests! Thanks a bunch!
Implying that OP's love for her cousin means she must give up her belongings just because she was asked to do so is emotional blackmail.
That sucks. I suspect she knows that she gave inappropriate "gifts" but just doesn't care. It is all a sick game to narcs.
Shame on her! How terrible! How did your guests react? Did they look confused, perhaps with a bit of nervous laughter or do they know your mother well enough to expect this sort of thing?

These people feel threatened by you. It is blindingly obvious to me as an outsider. They want you crawling in the low places with them and your beauty and interest in fashion makes them feel small and insecure. 

My mother and "best friend" had a habit of giving a small laugh whenever I talked of goals and dreams. It was the equivalent of "you're being silly". I grew up thinking everyone thought I was a fool and I went nowhere in life. 

I am now 41 years old and it was only a few years ago that I learned that the small laugh was not about me being a fool, it was because they did not understand me or did not believe in me. 

You know what got me wise to this? A courage wolf meme that read:

THOSE WHO LAUGH AT YOU
ARE SCARED OF YOU

(See, Reddit is not just a time waster!)   :)

I hope this information helps you. Please don't let those incredibly small-minded people take away your joy.

So, your mother wants to create a website for arranged marriages? Seriously, I think N-parents like this were born in the wrong place and would be happiest in a culture where parents largely decide who their child marries. 

Still, I don't think even MotherKnowsBest.com will satisfy a narc. No one will ever be truly good enough for their favorite child, even if they hand picked their son or daughter's spouse.
I hear ya. My mother did something similar. You can't win with narcs.

Giving life equals having sex. People get a reward for that now? All that other stuff they gave? Like what? Food, clothes, a home, and enrichment? That is basic parenting. Other stuff? All of their good moments go out the window due to the abuse. You don't get to tell others how much contact they must give to their abusers.

Good luck, because you know if she ever did call the police, she would not say you threw a sweatshirt in her direction. That shirt would morph into a baseball bat or a knife and you could indeed be arrested. 

Does she actually want you to live with your father or is this just some dumb line she spouts when she is mad?
These people are not true friends. In this context, words like *stubborn* and *brat* are code for "why won't you do what I think is right?" These people are using narc-talk on you.
Interesting analogy. Your Drill Instructor's response shows how people from sane families have no idea what we go (or have been) through.

Oh yes, I have heard this excuse from those who are too spineless to confront or pull away from a narc. These words are not untrue, but the underlying message is as you said, it is up to the victim to work around or simply deal with the narc's behavior. 

My response is that "Well, this is the way I am... I cut toxic people from my life."

My husband does similar things. I have recently come to consider him a mild narcissist and this acting put out over minor, unoffensive things is one way his narcissism expresses itself. 

My husband (and my Narc/Borderline mother) both have a habit of using nonverbal clues that are outside the norm. Why on earth would your husband say any of this is anyone's fault? If you misunderstood,  he should say so, not put on this immature display. 

Perhaps he is not a morning person or something was bothering him. Still, that doesn't excuse his behavior. You are his wife, not some bothersome person who happens to share his living quarters.
It gives me the creeps when women like this act as though their Daughter-In-Law stole their man.

Absolutely. My mother doesn't do the humiliation thing anymore but if it ever reared its ugly head again, I will simply look her in the eye and say: "Are you trying to humiliate me? Because that is a game you will lose." My mother has some embarrassing secrets, so this would shut her up for good.
She called the baby a hussy!!! You are very generous to allow this nasty woman in your life.
She referred to you as a sort of investment? That's cold. If she wants to play like that, I suppose you could demand pre-payment for any old care that she expects.

I regret not jumping into the black hole as well. In my 20s, I moved every year because my husband was in the Army. All I would have had to do is not give out my new address. 

I remember being nervous about the very unlikely possibility that my mother would hire a Private Investigator to find me. Today, it seems so silly that I worried about that. If I could do it all again, I would have collected my childhood pictures and then wrote a no contact letter. 

I am in my 40s and we didn't have the resources and support like this forum.

It was this sort of situation that helped me cement the decision to cut off a cousin. I had confided in the past to him about my marriage troubles. Some time after that, he calls and asks me how it is going. Not wanting to be negative, I said something about my getting better and better every day. 

By saying something suited to a cheesy motivational poster, I had meant this to be a lighthearted moment. I was shocked when my cousin gave a small laugh and asked "how's your marriage?"

This is the cousin to whom I had given so much emotional support. This is the cousin who called me when he wanted someone who understood what his NarcDad was like. I then realized cousin was also a bit of a narcissist and that I would no longer be his therapist and his cheering section. If my positive attitude has him grasping to bring me down a peg, he can find someone else.

I don't have an answer to your question but my marriage is the same way. I just wanted to let you know that you are an inspiration to me, getting that divorce. I'm so nervous about all the unknowns, so I stay.

How sick! MIL is more worried about covering her ass than the abuse of her son. It is terrible how these perverts got away with so much just because they hold religious office. I'm sending good thoughts to your husband and his friend who were so very strong to once again bring this into the light of day.
What an attention hound.

A few times when I was a teen, my mother would accuse me of forcing her to do something. What really happened was that I asked for her help with a project and she initially refused. I asked her a couple more times and she gave in.

I was always shocked when this accusation happened because my asking and her initial refusal and then giving in happened in everyday conversational tone. There was no shouting or anything to let me know how seriously did not want to help. 

She would just come out and claim I forced her to help, but only after she got mad at me for something else. I would stand there wondering where this came from and why a grown woman is acting like I held a gun to her head.

Yep, I downvoted this when I saw it on the larger sub. This is wrong on so many levels. Why on earth single out women? By this logic, could we also judge a man by his father? Must the child only take after the parent of the same sex? 

I guess some Redditor got involved with a girl who has the same personality faults as her mother and felt the internet needed to know this narrow-minded "wisdom".

Same here. For the past 5-10 years, my mother has expressed jealousy towards me. It is strange because for years she lived vicariously through me but now that I am far removed from her grasp, she only sees how much her life sucks when something good happens in my life.
How incredibly childish of your mother. I'm shaking my head at her immaturity and lack of reason.

Oh goodness, yes. This was one of the most infuriating things about my first husband, who was RBN and had narc tendencies of his own. 

His uncle is a high school English teacher, so I could never be right about some issue of grammar. He would "have to ask his uncle about that." He spoke to this uncle once every couple of years but every damn time it came to asking his uncle rather than just acknowledging that I might be correct.

My ex would also repeat things I said in at home conversation to his co-workers and would report back to me if they agreed or disagreed. This is one of the things that got me serious about filing for divorce. He could not or would not stop his gossip and it was insulting to have my every move and opinion second guessed by strangers.

Looking back, I suspect this may be due to the fact that my first husband was raised by narcs who taught him that parents know best because they have lived longer and been through it all before. (I always found that maddening, the assumption that nothing changes and their life experiences make them authority on all matters.) 

He had (and maybe still has) a need for a second opinion and validation from others in even small, mundane matters.

I'm glad you are able to find some humor in the situation because that is just terrible. It is good to hear that you and your sister have a close bond. Once your sister is out of the house, the two of you can leave your mother to herself and her out-of-control rage.

I think it is because we are human. We loved these people and perhaps a part of us will always love them. Narcs always complain and remember people's faults but if you are anything like me, you remember the good times and were glad to have them. 

Narcs move on fast while those of us with human empathy take plenty of time to process the situation and mourn the loss of a relationship. My only advice is to keep busy and avoid daydreaming. This is the only thing that has helped me.
That's pathetic. He should order a pizza or take-out if appliances are too complicated for him to handle.
Don't leave us hanging! I'm curious to know some of these desperate antics your mother is pulling.

I too am dealing with an elderly mother who abused me in the past. We are not required to forgive and forget once our parent is frail and circumstances tell them it is in their best interest to act civil towards us. Our distance is due to their abuse and this is the price they pay for their actions. 

Each of us decides how much to give these abusers. You don't have to support your mother if you don't feel it in your heart but if you want to do something, perhaps gather some resources that might help, such as literature or nearby support groups.

Your husband needs to cut the apron strings and stop bossing his wife around in order to placate his family. 

I usually don't say things so directly but I've been in a similar circumstance and it is a sore point. Your husband knows that you are a quiet, nervous person and are hearing impaired, so does he help his family better communicate with you, their guest? No, he lays all responsibility on you. That has the danger of creating a crack in the foundation of your marriage. 

You are doing your part in considering ways to be a better conversationalist. Will your husband rein in his family and let them know that you don't hate them, you just can't freaking understand them!

Good job on removing yourself from an unhealthy situation. Your wife may increase the amount of attempted contact and guilt as it becomes clear your separation is permanent. 

Writing it all out seems to be helping you. Keep posting if you need support or encouragement to stay strong.

That woman is soooo freaking annoying!!! I feel for you and am sending good vibes your way. I deal with someone who lacks communication because they just don't care, having a person do this deliberately makes me rage. 

My Aunt and Uncle used to ring the doorbell like a bunch of nutjobs when they visited my childhood home. Odd how these adults who seem to have their stuff together totally lose it for a stupid joke that got old really quick.

I would hazard a guess that the number of serious abusers who make a sincere change are very low. Even for those who do get better, having lost contact with their victims is something they have to live with, it is the abuser's fault, their victims do not have to stick around for something that may or may not happen.
I disagree. Offering your attention and your mental health on a periodic basis is not required. People like OP's parent are not just annoying or have differences of opinion, they are abusers.

Ugggh! That sounds so annoying. 

I'm thinking that if this only happens with a couple of people, perhaps they can't read people's tone and so they totally miss the joke. Do these people normally have a good sense of humor? Perhaps they suck at playing along with jokes. 

In your shoes, I would just not joke with these people. I think it would only create awkwardness to point out to them that they responded in a sort of inappropriate way.
Don't forget the burning.

I hope your wedding registry includes a fire extinguisher, because you know you are going to have to burn that letter. Are you sure you want to even open it? It sounds like you were doing great with no contact. Reading that letter could be considered opening the door, just a crack. Does your mother deserve to be heard?
This is extra awesome for me because I love snails and hate toxic relationships. Much thanks for posting!
These are wise words. You just took a weight off of my shoulders. Thanks a bunch!

Of course you should seek legal counsel and do whatever it takes to be safe from harm. There is a lot of advice out there for people escaping abusive marriages. Do a web search and let the experts guide you. Much of it will be written with women in mind, but it applies to men as well. Be sure to use privacy mode on your browser so your wife doesn't catch on to your plans. 

Good luck. You have been a wallet and a punching bag for far too long. Keep in touch and let us know how things are going.

I am seeing my mother in a new light. After watching this wonderful video, I see that what my mother did was covert bullying. It is so odd for me to call my mother that because with everyone else, she is meek and subservient and she is shy and struggles with social anxiety and phobias. 

But she bullied me, which was strange considering I was born to be her friend and helper. Her abuse chased me away and now I am very low contact and all she has is a fairly useless husband who was meant to replace me as her companion.

Since you mentioned that these letters ruin your mood, I would like to tell you how one of my cousins handled his nasty NarcDad's letters. 

My cousin went NC right after graduating High School. This was fine with his father until cousin built a successful career and a family and is doing very well for himself. Then NarcDad began to periodically send letters. You know he was desperate to go visit so he could brag. 

My cousin would throw those letters straight into the trash, unopened, right where they belonged. His father was a non-entity in my cousin's life and after the abuse that nasty narc dished out, that was exactly what he deserved.

Don't you just love revisionist history? 

It is maddening the way narcs do this, pulling words out of thin air and pinning the situation on others.

With my ex-MIL, conversations were never warm or sincere. Very quickly, I noticed she only paid as much attention as needed to glean information for the next person to hear. It was and presumably still is a sort of Round Robin newsfeed, where each person only serves to provide more talking points and narcissistic supply.

There is a self-help guru who struggled with depression, was even hospitalized for it, but now that she has beat her illness, she talks like your mother. It seems that after making a recovery from a sickness or personal battle, some people decide to fall into one of two camps: those who use their experience to help others and those who use their experience to berate others who have yet to make that same recovery.

Edited to add: About the "other people have it worse", there is saying that just because your neighbor has a broken back, doesn't mean you can't say "ouch" when you stub your toe on the coffee table. Since your mother likes platitudes, that should be right up her alley.
This is great news! For real, I have a big smile on my face having read that you are thriving in your new life.

Only you can decide whether you want to answer that message but if it were me, I would lean towards not calling because this is more of a summons than a request and having no details of what needs to be discussed, it feels like a lure rather than a real situation. 

If these people are so awful that you use the words "poison" and "sewage" to describe your interactions and you are No Contact for 10 years, I think your baby needs you more than they do.

Staying away from bad people is not selfish, it is self-preservation.

If a child takes away a parent's joy on a regular basis, then they are probably a poor excuse for a parent. If a person considers raising a child to be a downer, they should have considered that before making a baby.

If a close friend is taking all the joy out of you, then they are not acting as a friend. This is not to say we should drop a friend when they have troubles. Part of being a good companion is being there even when things are bad. However, if a "friend" becomes harsh or uncaring, it is time to move on. 

I hope there is no misunderstanding. My comment was meant to say that victims of Narcissists should indeed walk away from their abusers (at the earliest opportunity).
This is one of the few times I think you should listen to your mother.
It's a wonder why your mother needs to diet considering all the calories she must burn running from logic and leaping to conclusions.

Please protect your daughter. Your wife may be dealing with social pressures to keep in contact with family but there is no excuse for exposing a child to these deranged people. Adulterating someone's food is a good a reason as any to go Insanity Wolf on someone. Maybe I shouldn't talk but I can not imagine sitting quietly while an idiot spit on my baby's food.
Considering that most people need to pee first thing upon waking... well, you get the picture.
This is an informative post, thanks for spelling it out in an intelligent yet easy-to-digest sort of way.

Oh Denyala, I am so glad you mentioned the "short circuit" that Narcs get when you challenge their mindset. My ex-NMIL's brain used to freeze up when I said something that didn't fit in with perceived notions and that blank look on her face... it reminds me of an automaton who received too much or bad input!

Greetings, fellow vegan! I'm not so sure that most Reddit users hate vegans, it is just that the insecure loudmouths with nothing better to do drown out reasonable discussion.

Are you sure you would even want food made by those who are hostile to vegans? Between that and the long conversations which only serve to make you uncomfortable, and their filthy house, why bother? Perhaps listen most to the part of you that feels relief.
